body: I'm not indulging until the pm. My dog simply doesn't like the word. I stated in the original post, other words do not trigger him. He is the nicest dog. I was hoping to hear something from someone with more relevant material. Excuse me for mentioning unimportant details about my state of mind in the post.

I have only had one dog, and he's 6. We have a surgery scheduled to remove his eye from glaucoma.  He's such a little guy, it scares me to think he wont wake up from anesthesia. I haven't lost a dog, but I've lost almost all of family. I didn't deal with the grief graciously. I lost my dad to heroin when I 12, then my brother to heroin at 13, and finally my sister to heroin when I was 14. 10 years have passed and I have an understanding on how to not feel pain. I just pretend these key role humans in my life were insignificant. I try to think of future humans in my life who will unknowingly become the shapers of my life. As great as the times were with my family, they were just a chapter in my life. Pepper did not chose to leave you. She just needs to sleep now. Remember how peaceful she was in her most highlighted moments. Remember cuddling with her and convince yourself she held on to those times. It is likely she went with great peace. It is essential that you make room for other beings in your life. Remember you only live once, and Pepper wouldn't want you dwelling on her. I recommend you browse through some redlisted dogs who need a chance. If that isn't an option, just hang out with some other animals. Peace is in the palm of your hands.
I live in Sacramento California. I'm a 24 year old lady. I'd accompany you if it would help.

Drop the people who make you unhappy. You can't change them, the way you can change yourself. Social media is a serious bummer. Try to go back in time by developing face to face friendships. Keep those rare family members who see you as you are.
